title: Arc Length, Linear Velocity and Angular Velocity
seo_title: Precalculus Linear and Angular Velocity Worksheets (TEKS P.4D)
standard_text: P.4D represent angles in radians or degrees based on the concept of rotation in mathematical and real-world problems, including linear and angular velocity
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets for Texas TEKS P.4D: arc length, angular velocity, linear velocity, wheel speed and revolutions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: s = rθ and v = rω, with angles in radians.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Arc length: s = rθ, with θ in radians.
  • Angular velocity ω is the angle turned per unit of time. One revolution is 2π radians.
  • Linear velocity: v = rω, the distance a point on the edge travels per unit of time.
  • A rolling wheel moves one circumference, 2πr, per revolution.

Examples

Example

Radius 3 ft, 20 revolutions per minute

ω = 20 × 2π = 40π rad/min

v = 3 × 40π

Answer: 120π ≈ 377 ft per minute

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using degrees in s = rθChange to radians first.
Forgetting 2πRevolutions × 2π = radians.
Using the diameter as rHalve the diameter.

faq.q: Do all points on a wheel have the same angular velocity?
faq.a: Yes, but points farther from the center have greater linear velocity.

faq.q: What unit is angular velocity in?
faq.a: Radians (or revolutions or degrees) per unit of time.

faq.q: Why does radian measure make v = rω work?
faq.a: An angle of 1 radian cuts off an arc of length r.
